evidence.text: The 面 entry prints its reading and historical-form sequence, with cited examples labeled 商, 西周, 秦, 《說文》小篆, 漢, 戰國, and 楷書. Its account reports competing interpretations: the received 說文 explanation 从首 and “象人面形”; Li Xiaoding’s cited analysis describes the oracle form as 目 within a face-outline; the author says the oracle inscriptional context is fragmentary and 面’s use is unclear, and that the Western Zhou bronze form appears only as a component. The author describes the Chu-slip form as apparently derived from the Western Zhou form and the Qin, seal, and early Han forms as combining developments from oracle and Western Zhou shapes. This is the book author’s synthesis, not a claim that the source artifacts were independently examined.

evidence.text: The entry identifies 麪 as a phono-semantic graph: 麥 supplies meaning and 丏 supplies sound. It glosses the graph as fine powder made by grinding wheat, cites 說文 “麪，麦屑末也,” quotes 束皙’s “重羅之麪，尘飞雪白,” and reports 麵 as a colloquial spelling found in 集韻, with 面 as the current simplified spelling. It does not claim that the face word 面 supplied the flour word by borrowing.

evidence.field: discussion of proposed 面 component changes and limits, especially paragraphs 70–87
evidence.text: The article presents the eye-and-outline reading as the prevailing account it discusses, citing Li Xiaoding’s 甲骨文字集釋. It proposes possible pathways by which an eye-like element could be confused with head-related shapes, using comparisons of 目, 見, 頁, 首 and 𦣻. It explicitly treats these pathways as proposals and notes that no 面 bronze examples had been collected at the time. This supports recording disagreement and uncertainty about the graphic transition, not presenting one transformation pathway as settled.

evidence.text: The database interprets oracle 面 as an eye within an enclosing outline and gives face as the original sense. It reports 面 itself not attested in bronze inscriptions, though a bronze graph uses a related component with 𦣻 and an enclosure; it reports a Chu-slip enclosure altered toward 臼 and quotes a facing use from 上博楚竹書二《容成氏》簡14. These are database assertions and citations, not direct inspection of the artifact or slip.

evidence.field: A04763 麵, research and variant analysis
evidence.text: The entry identifies 麪 as the Shuowen form, analyzed 麥 plus 丏 phonetic, and describes 麵 as a later phono-semantic spelling with 麥 plus 面 sound and the same pronunciation and meaning. This is support for a 麪-to-麵 spelling relationship and for 面’s sound role in 麵; it does not show that the word for flour/noodles originated by borrowing the face word 面.

gaps: The 面 entry on 字源 p. 784 does not provide a firm chronological sequence connecting all listed graphic stages; it expressly says the oracle inscriptional context is fragmentary and the use unclear.

The local 《字源》 passages are direct scan inspections: PDF p. 797 / printed p. 784 for 面 and PDF p. 495 / printed p. 482 for 麪（面）. The adjacent PDF p. 798 / printed p. 785 page was also visually inspected to establish that it begins the next headword and does not continue the 面 account. Scan pixel hashes were verified against the supplied source_pixel_sha256 values.

The 字源 p. 784 account directly disputes any overconfident single-sequence learner wording: it distinguishes oracle 目 forms, Western Zhou component forms, Chu forms, and later mixed development, while reporting an unresolved relation. The original article glyph selection should remain unchanged per the task; no historical glyph replacement is proposed.

The source images show unusual historical forms as drawings. They are not assigned new Unicode identities here; no OCR correction is proposed because the relevant OCR prose and headwords match the inspected scans.

The dates of the oracle examples, the actual inscription contexts, and the argued 目-to-𦣻/首 transition mechanism remain unverified from artifact publications. The Fudan article offers possible mechanisms rather than demonstrating a single established path.
No first dated use was established for the senses ‘surface’, ‘side’, or ‘dimension’, nor a securely sourced semantic path linking those senses to face or facing.

麪’s 麥-plus-丏 analysis and 面’s later sound role in 麵 are supported. Exact chronology and earliest separate written attestations of flour and noodle senses were not resolved; do not infer that the face word 面 was borrowed to supply the food word.

The opened official policy resolution documents implementation of the general simplification scheme from 1956 but was not inspected here for the exact 面/麵 table line; use direct mapping evidence for that specific assertion if required.
